"Large language model inference on a single GPU is often limited less by arithmetic throughput than by the movement of tensors between high-bandwidth memory and the processor. In autoregressive decoding, each newly generated token requires a forward pass through the transformer, and the dominant cost is frequently the read of the key-value cache that stores the attention state for all previous tokens. This cache grows linearly with sequence length and batch size, and it must be accessed repeatedly as the model extends the sequence. Understanding speculative decoding, flash attention, and key-value cache traffic is therefore essential for predicting how a single GPU will behave under realistic serving workloads, because these three topics address different layers of the same problem: how to generate tokens quickly without exhausting memory bandwidth or capacity."
